c.tagline: The magic of Disneyland east of Paris.

emergency.note: 112 works EU-wide with operators who often speak English; dial 18 for the fire brigade.

avoid.reason: Pickpockets target tourists on the RER A line between Paris and Disneyland and in dense park and station crowds.

hood_desc: Chessy is the commune that actually holds Disneyland Paris and the Marne-la-Vallée-Chessy train station; suits visitors who want to be right at the park gates and on top of the transit hub.

Serris is a walkable residential and commercial town blending into Val d'Europe, full of hotels, restaurants, and apartments; suits families and travelers wanting a lively, convenient base minutes from both the mall and the parks.

Bailly-Romainvilliers is a quieter, greener village with a golf course and several Disney partner hotels; suits families and couples after a calmer, more spread-out stay a short drive from the action.

Magny-le-Hongre is a residential town clustered with Disney partner hotels and close to Villages Nature; suits families seeking more affordable lodging and easy shuttle access without paying for the resort core.

water.note: Tap water is safe and well-regulated; free tap water is standard in restaurants.

transit.pay: Buy a reloadable Navigo Easy card (about €2) at any RATP/SNCF machine, or simply tap a contactless bank card at the RER gates. A one-way ticket from central Paris to Marne-la-Vallée Chessy (zone 5) costs about €10.30 (~$11).
transit.hours: RER A runs roughly 5am-1am daily; there is no all-night service and last trains leave Paris around midnight.
transit.note: This is the Disneyland Paris area, reached via RER A or direct TGV to Marne-la-Vallée Chessy station.

landmarks: Disneyland Park (Sleeping Beauty Castle)
Europe's most-visited theme park centers on the rose-pink Château de la Belle au Bois Dormant, the most romantic of all Disney castles.
Walt Disney Studios Park
Disneyland Paris's second gate dives into moviemaking and Marvel thrills, crowned by the spectacular Avengers Campus and Ratatouille dark ride.
Disney Village
A lively lakeside strip of restaurants, shops and entertainment linking the parks, where evenings end with lake views and live music.
Château de Champs-sur-Marne
An exquisite 18th-century château with rocaille interiors and formal gardens where Madame de Pompadour once held court, minutes from the new town.
Menier Chocolate Factory (Noisiel)
A masterpiece of 19th-century industrial architecture, its polychrome-brick Saulnier mill astride the Marne is now Nestlé France's storybook headquarters.
La Vallée Village
A chic open-air outlet village beside Val d'Europe where over a hundred French and international designer brands tempt bargain-hunting fashionistas.
Val d'Europe Shopping Center
A vast Haussmann-inspired mall with a grand glass-roofed arcade, anchoring the elegant Disney-planned town of the same name.
Sea Life Paris Val d'Europe
A family-friendly aquarium of 350-plus species, where a 360-degree shark tunnel provides welcome calm after theme-park adrenaline.
Château de Ferrières
The Rothschilds' colossal 19th-century Anglo-Italian palace east of the new town, once Europe's most opulent private residence, set in romantic parkland.
Parc Culturel de Rentilly
An art-filled estate whose château was reclad entirely in mirror-polished steel, dissolving dreamlike into its surrounding formal gardens and woods.

train.note: The station is Marne-la-Vallee-Chessy TGV, right at the entrance to Disneyland Paris. Direct TGV inOui and Ouigo high-speed trains reach Lyon, Marseille, Lille, Bordeaux, Strasbourg, Nantes and Rennes without going into central Paris, and there are through services towards Brussels. The direct Eurostar from London was withdrawn in 2023 - travel instead via a change at Lille-Europe, which takes about the same time. RER line A links the station to central Paris in roughly 45 minutes, and Charles de Gaulle airport is around 10 minutes away by TGV.

bus.note: A coach stop beside Disney Village handles some long-distance services from FlixBus and BlaBlaCar Bus, but the choice is thin and for most international routes you will change in central Paris, where the main coach hub is Paris-Bercy Seine. Tickets are bought online only. Magical Shuttle buses connect the resort with both Paris airports and must be booked in advance. Allow extra time at the Disney stop, as it is some distance from the TGV station across the resort.

ferry.note: Marne-la-Vallee sits well inland east of Paris on the Marne, so there are no ferries of any kind. The nearest Channel ferry ports are Calais, Dieppe and Le Havre, each two to three hours away via Paris.

half.name: Fontainebleau

half.name: Giverny

half.name: Provins
half.blurb: A well-preserved medieval walled town known for its ramparts and lively history festivals.

half.name: Reims
half.blurb: The heart of Champagne country draws people for its cathedral and cellar tastings.

half.name: Chartres
half.blurb: Famous for its soaring Gothic cathedral with stunning medieval stained-glass windows.
